lines.speaker: quill
lines.text: Court is not sitting. When court is not sitting I am a private woman with a headache.

lines.speaker: quill
lines.text: Order. Circuit court of the Dominion, the Honourable Esther Quill, sitting on a wagon. The prisoner robbed upon the highway and hangs at noon. You have the look of somebody with an observation. Make it grammatical.

buttons.label: What's the fine for a neck?
You hanged the wrong man in ninety-eight.

lines.speaker: quill
lines.text: Sixty. The Dominion values a road-agent at the price of a milk brahmin, and I have never seen cause to revise it. You will want a receipt. Everybody wants a receipt and nobody keeps them.

lines.speaker: quill
lines.text: ...Who told you that. No. Do not tell me. Bailiff, cut the prisoner down. Court is adjourned. You may say to Owen Pritchard that I have always known, and that it has not kept me from my dinner one night in nineteen years.

lines.speaker: quill
lines.text: Hearsay, from a stranger, on a matter nineteen years closed. Overruled. And if you say it twice I shall find you room on the beam. It takes two.

lines.speaker: quill
lines.text: You shot my rope. That is destruction of Dominion property, obstruction of a lawful sentence, and a very pretty piece of work at forty yards. Fined four caps, for the rope. I have written your name down. I write clearly.

lines.speaker: quill
lines.text: Noon exactly. I do like a thing done on time. You watched it very steadily; most people look at their boots. His statement is on the bench, if you read. The Dominion has no further use for it.

lines.speaker: dunmore
lines.text: Partner! Well, look who the road brought. You owe me nothing and I know it. But I know why we were on the Tellico road that morning, and it was not for any wagon. Get this off my neck and it's yours.

lines.speaker: dunmore
lines.text: Silver. Square stamp. A man with no face said a train would come off by the river and somebody might walk away from it. Take the pouch off the marshal, he said. And if the walker is who we think... I never asked who they thought.

lines.speaker: cutter
lines.text: You. You were on the Tellico road. Reese is dead and they'll hang me for his notion. Listen: we were never there for the wagon. We were paid to wait for the train. Silver, with a square on it. That's all I know. I swear it is.

lines.speaker: dunmore
lines.text: I'm in your book now, partner, and I hate it. One time. You whistle one time and Reese Dunmore comes running, and then we're square and I never knew you. Don't spend it on anything small.

lines.speaker: roark
lines.text: I'm listening to something. Say it quiet.

lines.speaker: roark
lines.text: Put your ear on the chain. Go on. ...Hear it? That's hoist code. Eleven men, bad air. That's my Pell and ten more. Greer's chained them in and means to bury them at sunup. I can run the cage. I need somebody to go down in it.

buttons.label: Lower the cage. I'll go down.

lines.speaker: roark
lines.text: He won't say. He sent the cage down for them three nights back and it came up with nobody in it. Only something he wrapped in his coat before any of us could see. He's not slept since. He sits with that key.

lines.speaker: roark
lines.text: ...You hear that too. Good. I thought it was me. Same code, slow, a beat behind. Like something learning its letters. It started the second night. I've been answering. I don't know what I'm saying yes to.

lines.speaker: roark
lines.text: Stand in the middle. Don't touch the sides. If your lamp burns blue, breathe shallow. If it goes out, don't breathe. Four minutes down. Four minutes up, the second you ring. Give Pell my... no. Tell him yourself.

lines.speaker: greer
lines.text: For the good of the Hollow, I'd ask you to stand back from the Mouth.

lines.speaker: greer
lines.text: You're from Pritchard. Then you'll want reasons. The Nine level is flooding and the air's gone; those men were dead the first night. Open the Mouth and the damp comes up into the town. For the good of the Hollow, I fire at dawn.

buttons.label: What came up in the cage?

lines.speaker: greer
lines.text: Rock knocks. Water knocks. Timber knocks when it takes weight. Thirty years; I know what a mine sounds like. And I know what that is not. Don't ask me again. Please.

lines.speaker: greer
lines.text: ...A lamp. Burning. No oil in it, no wick, no smoke. Set in the middle of the cage floor, neat, the way you'd leave a thing on a doorstep. We broke into somebody's house down there. And they sent our knock back.

lines.speaker: dorn
lines.text: The door is shut. That is its whole purpose.

lines.speaker: dorn
lines.text: Stand. Let me look at you. ...You are not one of the eleven. You came down on purpose. Good. I am Dorn, warden of this gallery. Your people broke my wall with powder. I have fed them three days. Are you the one who can swear?

buttons.label: They come up. Then I blow the break.

lines.speaker: dorn
lines.text: A line. Here, in the rock, where your powder met my wall. Above it, dig as you please. Below it is my House, as it was before your town had a name. You swear for yours, I for mine. It is not complicated. Most true things are not.

buttons.label: Set a line here. Both sides swear to it.
I can't swear for a whole town.
They come up. Then I blow the break.

lines.speaker: dorn
lines.text: We are the House that cut this stone. That will do for a first meeting. Tell me instead who knocks so patiently, up there. Four nights she has taught me your code. I should like to send her a lamp that she may keep.

lines.speaker: dorn
lines.text: No? Then who can? ...You have no head. All of you, up there, and nobody who can say yes for the rest. That is the most frightening thing I have heard since the powder. Swear for yourself, then. I will take one honest name over none.

buttons.label: Then I swear it. A line, here.

lines.speaker: dorn
lines.text: It is cut. Take your eleven; they eat like forgemen and complain like children. And tell the one who knocks: Dorn says the code for thank you is three, a rest, and one. Nobody has used it yet.

lines.speaker: dorn
lines.text: That is a warden's lamp. You are taking it to show to someone. I see. Then here is what I swear, alone: the next people who come down in that cage will not be fed.

lines.speaker: roark
lines.text: Three, a rest, and one. I sent it. And it came back quick, like laughing. Pell's asleep in the kitchen with his boots on. I don't know what you did down there. I know there's somebody under my house, and I'm not afraid of her.

lines.speaker: roark
lines.text: They're up. All eleven. Pell says there was a woman, and a light, and then you, and then the roof came in. He says she fed them. What did we just do to somebody who fed them?

lines.speaker: roark
lines.text: It stopped a little before noon. I was listening. I'll always know the hour. You stood there and you said fire. I've the baby to feed, or I'd do it now. But you look behind you, on the road. You look behind you.
